findings.text: Universal tags occupy values zero through thirty one, with fourteen and fifteen reserved. Zero marks end of contents, early values cover boolean, integer, bit and octet strings, null, identifier and descriptive types, later values cover time, sequence, set and many string flavors, and thirty one signals long tag form. Indefinite length uses a single byte with only the top bit set, namely 0x80.

Decoding state holds a pointer to immutable bytecode, the length of that bytecode, and a pointer to a table of action callbacks. Each action returns integer status and receives an opaque caller context as its first argument; further parameters are not shown in the visible fragment.

Matching opcodes separate unconditional matches from conditional matches, with orthogonal options to skip on mismatch, run an action, transfer control, accept any tag, or evaluate conditionally. A threshold marks the end of tag consuming operations. Remaining operations report failure, completion, unconditional or optional actions, sequence and set closure with set, collection and action variants, and return from nested matching.

Matching modifiers use distinct low bits for skip, action invocation, jump, wildcard tag and conditional gating. Closure modifiers distinguish set from sequence, collection of from singular, and whether an action runs. Small constructors pack class, construction and tag number into a match byte, encode raw tags, designate jump destinations and index the action table.

Asynchronous work uses a sixty four bit cookie and a callback taking opaque data plus the cookie. A domain object contains a pending list and a single bit flag for shared versus exclusive ownership. Two declaration helpers produce a statically initialized domain differing only in that flag, one for shared use and one for exclusive use.

Four wrappers choose placement and domain association before delegating. The plain and domain forms request no specific node, while device forms derive placement from the given device. Domain accepting forms forward the caller domain; others use the default domain.
Device node lookup is build dependent. One variant returns the identifier stored in the device object, the other always indicates no preference. Callers must accept either outcome.
Channel reference entries store a channel pointer, list linkage, deferred cleanup state and an atomic use count, supporting shared lookup with safe reclamation.
Transaction flags assign separate low bit positions to zeroing the destination, dropping the destination, acknowledging the descriptor, fencing later work and handling parity destinations.

Submission control bundles flags, an optional predecessor descriptor, a completion callback with opaque argument and a scratch pointer. A companion union overlays a machine address, page pointer and DMA address in one word. An initializer copies caller supplied flag, dependency, callback, argument and scratch values into the control block.

Issue and lookup behavior splits by configuration. The active configuration maps global issue to the DMA layer, delivers a present single descriptor to the owning channel device for issue, and looks up channels from dependency and type. The inert configuration performs no issue work and reports no channel, implying synchronous fallback by the caller.
Synchronous completion only notifies when a callback was provided, passing through the stored argument and otherwise remaining silent.

An auxiliary device embeds a generic device, a name pointer, a small numeric identity, a sysfs area with an interrupt table, a mutex and a directory presence flag, plus an opaque field for external registration data.

An auxiliary driver provides probe, removal, shutdown, suspend and resume handlers, where probe also receives the matched table entry. It stores a name string, an embedded generic driver and a pointer to its identifier table.

Driver data helpers exchange opaque pointers through the embedded generic device storage. Device and driver conversions recover the enclosing auxiliary object from the embedded generic object with a compile time compatibility check.

Device addition, driver registration, managed creation and module declaration forward to internal helpers while supplying the compilation module name and, for managed creation, platform data and identifier seed. Uninitialization tears down sysfs synchronization and drops the device reference, while deletion detaches the device without dropping the reference.
Interrupt sysfs registration in this configuration always indicates success with no effect, and deregistration does nothing, showing the optional feature compiled out.
The sysfs mutex guards creation of interrupt sysfs entries and the associated presence flag, so concurrent setup cannot race directory creation.
The base auxiliary vector size is twenty four (24) entries. Base64 handling offers standard, URL safe and IMAP alphabets, and the character count for a byte length grows as four thirds rounded up.

The moving average generator creates a per name accumulator with initialization, read and update helpers. Precision and reciprocal weight must be compile time constants, precision has a small upper bound and weight must be a power of two. Reads scale down by precision. Updates blend the scaled sample with prior state according to the reciprocal, seeding directly when empty, using single copy accesses for the shared field.
Backing file context keeps a credential pointer for lower file operations and two optional hooks, one on access and one on write completion carrying the I/O context and transferred length.

Each bad block word packs sector offset in middle bits, length minus one in low bits and acknowledgement in the highest bit. Maximum single run length is five hundred twelve (512) sectors. Table capacity equals page size divided by eight byte entries. Helpers derive offset, length, acknowledgement state, end position and assembled words.

Bad block state records the owning device, population count, a hint that unacknowledged entries may exist, a sector to block shift where negative disables tracking, a pointer to the entry array, a changed marker, a sequence lock and the covered sector start and size. A scan context carries start, length and acknowledgement intent.

Capacity and emptiness checks inspect the population count. Changed markers only transition between set and clear states. Managed teardown verifies the instance belongs to the caller device, issuing a single driver warning and stopping on mismatch, otherwise invoking core release.

Balloon state tracks a count of isolated pages, a queue of pages lent to the host, an optional migration handler taking balloon state, new and old pages plus mode, and a flag for managed count adjustment. Initialization clears the count and handler, empties the queue and disables adjustment.

Packed decimal helpers choose compile time evaluation for constant inputs and runtime helpers otherwise. Validity demands both nibbles stay within decimal range. Decoding adds the low nibble to ten times the high nibble; encoding splits tens into the high nibble and units into the low.

BCH parameters include field order, code length, correction capability and redundancy sizes in bits and bytes, followed by private tables for exponentiation, logarithms, modular reduction, syndrome work areas, caches, locator polynomials and a bit order option. Identifier length means the number of thirty two bit elements in the array.

Host attachment distinguishes PCI, SDIO and on chip system integration. Chip identity combines numeric id, revision and package; board identity combines vendor and type. Clock mode selects fast or dynamic operation. Host operations abstract narrow loads and stores, optional block moves qualified by register width, and separate agent space accesses.

Stable identifiers cover three manufacturers, seven functional classes and a large core catalog plus invalid, default and sizing sentinels. Manufacturers span ARM, MIPS and Broadcom values. Classes span simulation, ROM, debug, verification, optimization, generic and prime cell. Cores span chipcommon, memory, CPU, interconnect, network, wireless, storage, serial, audio, USB, SDIO and Northstar family functions. Representative codes include 0x43B, 0x4A7 and 0x4BF for manufacturers, 0x0, 0x1, 0x9, 0xB, 0xD, 0xE and 0xF for classes, and 0x367 and 0x800 for out of band routing and chipcommon.

Nullable descriptors, unlocked count and flag inspection, and build time constraints on averaging parameters create caller obligations. Issuing with a null descriptor must be tolerated, count and changed flag reads can race without the sequence lock, and invalid precision or weight stops compilation.

Enclosing object recovery enforces pointer type compatibility at compile time, rejecting mismatched member use. Asynchronous offload inlining differs by configuration, so code must not rely on a particular linkage or expansion of the helpers.
